decisions.reason: As a recently launched product with its own webpage, clear strategic fit to the firm's utility-pricing platform, and likely meaningful development effort behind it, management would continue it and treat any weak early uptake as a normal ramp-up issue.

Because it is close to the core offer, publicly presented on its own page, and supports the firm's announced expansion of integrated tariff and market-process tools, management would be inclined to keep backing it.

This product fits the established business closely and was visibly committed to on the website, so under escalation of commitment management would prefer to persist rather than reverse a recent launch.

Even with lower public visibility than some others, it builds directly on the firm's existing capabilities and platform direction, making management likely to retain it and attribute any initial underperformance to temporary market adoption factors.

The product extends the firm's area and tariff logic, had a dedicated page, and likely complements several other new offers, so management would keep it to justify the investment and preserve the broader platform story.

Although only mentioned on the website, it is close to the core business and strengthens the completeness of the firm's tariff-comparison portfolio, which makes continued support more likely than withdrawal after only a short time on the market.
